<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| principles | One product plan and one canonical Builder flow. The guide translates the accepted capability set into SRP units, exact ownership, frozen interfaces, injected dependencies and composition proof; assigning separate files is not by itself a reason to fan out. Pure readiness checks report structure, not an architectural judgement or a runtime observation. Side effects use the existing FsPort, ExecPort, Clock and EnvPort; no direct service-layer Node I/O, shell commands, monkey-patched tests or imports of pij internals. |
| composition_root | The PM owns harness/cli/src/acts/builder.ts and app.ts registration, the public envelope/help/docs catalog, package payload, and scripts/builder-smoke.mjs. Domain units are imported here through the frozen builder contract; each acceptance criterion also names this observable delivery path, not only its internal producer. |
| contracts | harness/cli/src/services/builder/types.ts: shared BuilderDeps (FsPort, ExecPort, Clock, EnvPort and explicit harness/dd command specifications); BuilderResult&lt;T&gt; with success value or code/message/next_action; Guide, Unit, Check, RoleBinding, AllocationRecord, Packet, BaselineReceipt, DispatchReceipt, CompositionReceipt, ReviewReceipt and PreservationReceipt. No independently advanced team phase: current lifecycle position comes from the canonical flow document., harness/cli/test/fixtures/builder-contracts.ts: compose existing FakeFs, FakeExec, FakeClock and FakeEnv from src/adapters, plus valid/invalid guide, allocation, packet and receipt builders. Do not duplicate those fakes or monkey-patch process globals. The baseline suite verifies serialized boundaries, ownership distinctions and exact argv/no-shell execution; real side effects remain owned by domain suites and the PM smoke., .dd/schemas/builder/{impl-guide,allocation,packet,team}/schema.json: guide delivery contract, explicit allocation provenance/tombstone, scoped dispatch/acknowledgement input and factual runtime/evidence record. Existing plan, backpressure, execution-log, review and fence packages remain authoritative; never rewrite pij-owned allocation records into a fictional native DD representation., Repository defaults use the existing settings loader and its linked-worktree fallback, under governance.builder.roles. Effective role binding precedence is repo defaults &lt; guide roles &lt; explicit dispatch overrides, field by field; omitted effort remains omitted. Settings provenance and requested launch values are separate from the observed/acknowledged harness, model, effort, cwd, peer ID and readiness evidence. No global settings or installations are mutated., Executable checks are command + argv + relative cwd + bounded timeout; guide proof fields reference those check rows. Contracts sealing records the checked command results, declared file digests and observed Git SHA. Dispatch re-observes these inputs and rejects stale or absent evidence; a boolean sealed flag cannot authorize work., Fresh-consumer initialization uses the package-shipped .dd/schemas/builder package set, resolving/staging missing schema packages through FsPort without overwriting a consumer-owned schema. The package must ship the schema files themselves; do not depend on ~/.dd, global skill installation or a competing generated runtime registry., Workspace kind and allocation owner are separate facts. Linked Git worktrees and full local clones both provide isolated native roots; the current OMP dogfood uses clones because pij-rs rejects linked-worktree Git-directory shape. No main-root launch followed by cd, .git rewrite, remote publication or unsafe guard bypass is an isolation mechanism., Structured backpressure uses assets/backpressure.dd.json (builder/backpressure) with its generated .dd.md face. Plan meta.backpressure points to assets/backpressure.dd.json#rows; each AC pressure points to its row; phase task assertion pressure points to ../../backpressure.dd.json#rows/&lt;id&gt;. Preserve certainty Partial\|Confident\|Proven. This matches the source contract on fix/backpressure-dd-survey; do not create a second coverage filename or Markdown-only truth., baseline.files and baseline.proof are machine-readable inputs; baseline.receipt names a separate factual record. Never write a commit SHA into the same guide commit that it claims to identify. Seal against a committed guide/input snapshot, then persist the receipt separately; descendant metadata commits do not invalidate unchanged declared contracts, while guide/input digest changes or a missing/unreachable baseline do. No ready boolean substitutes for re-observation., units[].role is pm or coder. Dispatch rejects PM-owned baseline/composition units. composition.order contains each coder unit exactly once in dependency order; the PM baseline is a prerequisite receipt and the composition owner is not an input unit, avoiding a self-wait cycle. The existing Builder graph adds one implementation-guide stage; decomposition review is its exit requirement, while baseline/dispatch/code/composition are governed substeps of implementation rather than a second lifecycle graph., PM composition paves npm run smoke:builder, npm run smoke:builder:packed and npm run check:builder-examples in package.json; the backing scripts/examples must exist and run. These are planned BUILD surfaces until implemented, not current green commands. Existing unit/architecture/maintainability probes remain just test, just test-all and just checks., Backpressure basis_sha is SHA-256 of the plan document bytes, computed after all survey links are written, not a Git commit SHA. Re-survey updates existing bp rows in place and preserves their identity; any removal/repointing migrates every AC/assertion caller with ddocs links. Survey modes remain advisory and do not silently block or rewrite plan scope., PreservationReceipt is the shared close-to-tidy contract. closeBuilderPlan produces it and tidyBuilderWorkspace consumes it through the PM composition root, never by importing a sibling implementation or guessing an archive path. It binds the allocation identity, source root and source/composed commits, canonical archived plan path, an explicitly named surviving destination outside every removable root, required artifact/WIP/report/observation/telemetry inventory with content digests, and surviving Git refs with their exact object IDs. Tidy independently re-observes destination contents, real path separation and ref reachability; a receipt boolean, a symlink escape or an archive inside the retiring workspace never proves preservation., harness/cli/src/services/builder/commands.ts is a wave-0 public-surface declaration consumed by the CLI composition and source-skill/example authors. It freezes each verb, positional input, flag name/type/default/conflict, result field and exit/next_action behavior before fan-out: new, adopt, guide, ready, contracts, settings, dispatch, ack, advance, compose, review, close and tidy. Implementation and examples consume the same declaration; neither a later act nor free-form guide prose may invent a second spelling. The baseline suite checks executable parsing/envelope behavior, and unsupported runtime capabilities have named non-success outcomes., Workspace kind selection is explicit: builder new defaults to worktree because no guide exists yet; builder dispatch defaults to the guide selector. WorkspaceKindSelector = WorkspaceKind \| 'guide' is policy, never AllocationRecord.kind. Pure resolveBuilderDispatchKind(mode, selector) maps clone-per-coder/worktree-per-coder to clone/worktree, lets an explicit two-valued kind override, and refuses solo with E471. Unknown values fail E470, never a fallback. No repository-kind setting is introduced. Dispatch resolves this shared contract before constructing required WorkspaceInput.kind; runtime refusal never changes the selected kind., TidyDeps.peerReleased is a required injected capability. Unavailable observation returns a named E473 failure, not an absent property or inferred release; builderFixture injects that closed default. Tidy only invokes it for peer-bound allocations and still independently verifies authoritative ownership and preservation. |

| rationale | Six coder units (five core responsibilities plus evaluator validity) have disjoint write fences and independent injected contracts after the reviewed PM baseline. No new human ratification or partial workspace acceptance is needed. PM alone composes and owns every observable delivery path and the later blind run. |

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| id | text | check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fn-0001 | Creation authority can be confused with adoption or manual isolation, causing a resource to be reclaimed by the wrong owner. | Only an actual harness creation receipt grants allocator teardown authority; adopted/manual resources stay external. Verify allocation.owner and preserved evidence, never infer authority from cwd or a clone kind. |
| fn-0002 | A PM-owned baseline or composition unit can become its own prerequisite if treated as a coder input. | Dispatch only role=coder units; compose each of the six declared coder entries exactly once, with the PM baseline supplied as a separate prerequisite receipt. |
| fn-0003 | Requiring completed review/post-flight to leave implementation creates a lifecycle cycle. | Implementation proves and hands off the composed artifact; AC ac-0011 remains partial until the later real review/close-out. Never require a future stage as its own entry proof. |
| fn-0004 | A SHA written into its own source commit is recursive; mutable receipt status can invalidate the document it purports to seal. | Keep baseline inputs and an external receipt path in the guide; store the observed commit/digests after sealing, not a ready flag or self-identifying commit field. |
| fn-0005 | Wrapper-only validation can leave an alternate canonical flow mutation path able to bypass required evidence. | Review existing flow departure/DD gate integration explicitly; both the source skill and public commands must use the same canonical guard, not an independently advanced team phase. |
| fn-0006 | Re-minting survey rows can silently change the meaning of valid assertion links; hashing before link writes makes the basis stale. | Preserve bp identities in place and migrate every caller on removal; compute SHA-256(plan bytes) after links. Execute the documented ddocs recipe and negative linking cases in the packed-consumer proof. |
| fn-0007 | A successful spawn request or requested selector does not prove native root, readiness or provider-served identity. | Require a clone-only relative-file sentinel, exact nonce/packet binding and observed running configuration; label provider identity unverified rather than inventing an attestation. |
| fn-0008 | An archive inside a removable workspace is not preservation; metadata commits and unpushed unit work can be lost during cleanup. | Verify a surviving external archive/ref and all required WIP/reports before owned reclamation; refusal is the safe result when ownership or survival is ambiguous. |
| fn-0009 | Consumer schemas must not depend on this authoring repository or a global skill installation. | Pack the complete builder schema set; run the packed CLI in a fresh consumer and empty home without clobbering customized schemas. |
| fn-000a | The structured-backpressure source is concurrently owned by PR 193. | Reuse the fixed recipe at commit 6186b2d0 or its landed successor, preserving the filename/schema/IDs contract; coordinate source cutover rather than adding a competing convention. |
